Continue from [Compositional analysis](compositional_analysis.html). This article answers the question: does ageing change transcription in lung epithelial cells?

Epithelial cells are integrated with Harmony, clustered into six populations, and aggregated to sample-level pseudobulk profiles. DESeq2, through [tidybulk](https://github.com/stemangiola/tidybulk), tests one epithelial cluster for age-associated genes, adjusting for study and cell count [@love2014deseq2]. Those genes form an epithelial ageing signature, which is scored on individual cells with [singscore](https://github.com/DavisLaboratory/singscore) to show where the transcriptional change sits across the epithelium [@foroutan2018singscore].

The reusable script for everything you have run is installed with the package:

```{r, eval=FALSE, cache=FALSE}
file.edit(system.file(
  "scripts", "workshop_respiratory_ageing.R",
  package = "cellNexusWorkshop"
))
```

## Split the broad epithelial label

`epithelial` is one broad label. Ciliated, secretory, basal, and alveolar cells all sit inside it, so a single expression average mixes cell types that are not the same. The test therefore splits those cells into smaller clusters, and uses marker genes to decide whether that split is a real set of smaller cell types. A cluster is identified by the genes that mark it.

## Integrate epithelial cells and define six clusters

Epithelial cells are integrated with Harmony and cut into six clusters. The age test uses the cluster that can support the design. This example uses 12,000 epithelial cells. [Harmony](https://github.com/immunogenomics/harmony) here is for clustering and the UMAP. The counts still carry study effects, and the model below still includes `dataset_id`.

```{r, include=FALSE, eval=TRUE}
obs_lung <- readRDS(
  system.file("extdata", "obs_lung.rds", package = "cellNexusWorkshop")
)
```

```{r eval=FALSE}
epi_cell_cap <- 12000L
min_cells_pb <- 10L

set.seed(42)
epi_cells <- obs_lung |>
  dplyr::filter(cell_type_unified_ensemble == "epithelial")
epi_cells <- dplyr::slice_sample(
  epi_cells,
  n = min(epi_cell_cap, nrow(epi_cells))
)

sce_epi <- epi_cells |>
  get_single_cell_experiment(assays = "counts") |>
  logNormCounts()

hvgs <- sce_epi |>
  modelGeneVar() |>
  getTopHVGs(n = 2000)

sce_epi <- sce_epi |>
  runPCA(ncomponents = 30, subset_row = hvgs) |>
  RunHarmony(
    group.by.vars = "dataset_id",
    dims.use = 1:30,
    verbose = FALSE,
    reduction.save = "HARMONY"
  ) |>
  runUMAP(dimred = "HARMONY", n_neighbors = 15)

sce_epi$epi_cluster <- factor(paste0(
  "E",
  clusterCells(
    sce_epi,
    use.dimred = "HARMONY",
    BLUSPARAM = KmeansParam(centers = 6L)
  )
))
# base::saveRDS(sce_epi, "./inst/extdata/sce_epi.rds", compress = "xz")
```

```{r epi-umap, eval=FALSE}
sce_epi |>
  ggplot(aes(UMAP1, UMAP2, colour = epi_cluster)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.3, alpha = 0.6) +
  coord_equal() +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r epi-umap-plot, echo=FALSE, eval=TRUE}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(
  dirname(knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE)),
  "..", "man", "figures", "epi-umap.png"
))
```

## Aggregate sample-by-cluster pseudobulk

Each later test treats the sample as the replicate. `aggregateAcrossCells.se()` sums raw counts within each sample and cluster. The column `ncells` is the number of cells that entered each pseudobulk. Profiles with fewer than 10 cells are dropped. `log_cell_count` is a scaled depth covariate so profiles built from different numbers of cells are comparable.


```{r eval=FALSE}
pb_se <- scrapper::aggregateAcrossCells.se(
  sce_epi,
  factors = list(
    sample_id = sce_epi$sample_id,
    epi_cluster = sce_epi$epi_cluster
  ),
  counts.name = "ncells"
)

SummarizedExperiment::assayNames(pb_se)[
  SummarizedExperiment::assayNames(pb_se) == "sums"
] <- "counts"

pb_se <- pb_se |>
  dplyr::filter(ncells >= min_cells_pb) |>
  dplyr::mutate(log_cell_count = as.numeric(scale(log1p(ncells))))

pb_se
```

```{r include=FALSE, eval=TRUE}
pb_se <- readRDS(file.path(
  dirname(knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE)),
  "..", "inst", "extdata", "pb_se.rds"
))
pb_se
```

## Test one cluster for age-associated genes

This section asks which genes change expression with age inside one epithelial population.

### Choose a cluster that can support the age term

k-means labels change with the seed and the cell cap, so the cluster for the age model is chosen from a screen. A cluster qualifies when both age classes have enough cells and samples, neither class is a small fraction of the cluster, at least two studies contribute both age classes, and the design matrix has full rank. Full rank means age can be separated from study: if every study in a cluster supplies only one age class, the age coefficient cannot be separated from `dataset_id`. Eligible clusters are sorted by how many studies span both ages, then by the number of pseudobulk profiles. The first row is the cluster that is tested. The thresholds here are 150 cells and 5 samples in each class. If the screen has no eligible row, lower a threshold and rebuild it.

```{r}
de_design <- ~ age_binary + log_cell_count + dataset_id

min_cells_per_class <- 150L
min_samples_per_class <- 5L
min_cell_fraction <- 0.25
min_datasets_spanning_age <- 2L

epi_cluster_screen <- as.data.frame(SummarizedExperiment::colData(pb_se)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    epi_cluster = as.character(epi_cluster),
    is_old = as.logical(age_binary)
  ) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    n_pseudobulk = dplyr::n(),
    n_cells = sum(ncells),
    n_cells_young = sum(ncells[!is_old]),
    n_cells_old = sum(ncells[is_old]),
    n_samples_young = dplyr::n_distinct(sample_id[!is_old]),
    n_samples_old = dplyr::n_distinct(sample_id[is_old]),
    n_datasets = dplyr::n_distinct(dataset_id),
    n_datasets_spanning_age = sum(
      tapply(is_old, factor(as.character(dataset_id)), dplyr::n_distinct) == 2L,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    .by = epi_cluster
  )

epi_cluster_screen$full_rank <- vapply(
  epi_cluster_screen$epi_cluster,
  function(cl) {
    se <- pb_se[, pb_se$epi_cluster == cl]
    se <- se[, Matrix::colSums(SummarizedExperiment::assay(se, "counts")) > 0]
    cd <- droplevels(as.data.frame(SummarizedExperiment::colData(se)))
    mm <- try(stats::model.matrix(de_design, data = cd), silent = TRUE)
    !inherits(mm, "try-error") && qr(mm)$rank == ncol(mm)
  },
  logical(1)
)

epi_cluster_screen <- epi_cluster_screen |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    frac_young = n_cells_young / pmax(n_cells, 1),
    frac_old = n_cells_old / pmax(n_cells, 1),
    eligible =
      n_cells_young >= min_cells_per_class &
      n_cells_old >= min_cells_per_class &
      n_samples_young >= min_samples_per_class &
      n_samples_old >= min_samples_per_class &
      frac_young >= min_cell_fraction &
      frac_old >= min_cell_fraction &
      n_datasets_spanning_age >= min_datasets_spanning_age &
      full_rank
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(
    dplyr::desc(eligible),
    dplyr::desc(n_datasets_spanning_age),
    dplyr::desc(n_pseudobulk),
    epi_cluster
  )

if (!any(epi_cluster_screen$eligible)) {
  stop(
    "No epithelial cluster can support this design. ",
    "Clusters are either too small, too unbalanced, or their studies each ",
    "supply a single age class."
  )
}

epi_cluster_de_top <- epi_cluster_screen$epi_cluster[[1]]
epi_cluster_screen
```

> **Exercise 7.** From `epi_cluster_screen`, which cluster was chosen? How many studies in that cluster contribute both age classes (`n_datasets_spanning_age`)? Quote the screen table with the result. The label alone is not reproducible.

<details>
<summary>Solution</summary>

```r
epi_cluster_de_top
epi_cluster_screen
```

The chosen row is the first row of the screen after eligible clusters are sorted by `n_datasets_spanning_age`, then by the number of pseudobulk profiles. Quote `n_datasets_spanning_age` for that row. A value of 1 means the age term rests on a single study.

</details>

### Test old against young with DESeq2

The contrast is old versus young: positive log fold changes are higher in donors over 50. DESeq2 tests against a log2 fold change of 1, so the p-value asks whether the change exceeds a doubling. Say that when you report the p-values. `sfType = "poscounts"` estimates size factors on sparse pseudobulk, where the default median-of-ratios estimator can find no gene detected in every profile.

Genes are kept when they reach 5 counts per million in at least half of the profiles, evaluated with respect to age, so a gene expressed in one age class survives.

```{r}
pb_se <- pb_se[, pb_se$epi_cluster == epi_cluster_de_top]
pb_se <- pb_se[, Matrix::colSums(assay(pb_se, "counts")) > 0]

assay(pb_se, "counts") <- round(assay(pb_se, "counts"))
pb_se$sizeFactor <- NULL

pb_se$age_binary <- factor(
  ifelse(pb_se$age_binary, "old", "young"),
  levels = c("young", "old")
)

pb_se <- pb_se |>
  keep_abundant(
    formula_design = ~ age_binary,
    minimum_proportion = 0.5,
    minimum_count_per_million = 5
  ) |>
  test_differential_expression(
    de_design,
    contrasts = list(c("age_binary", "old", "young")),
    method = "DESeq2",
    omit_contrast_in_colnames = TRUE,
    test_above_log2_fold_change = 1,
    sfType = "poscounts"
  ) |>
  adjust_abundance(
    .factor_unwanted = c(log_cell_count, dataset_id),
    .factor_of_interest = age_binary,
    method = "limma_remove_batch_effect"
  )
```

### Plot the genes in the ageing signature

The signature uses a nominal p-value cutoff, capped at 25 genes in each direction. It is a gene set for scoring. A claim about an individual gene needs the false-discovery column as well. Report both. The boxplots show those genes after `adjust_abundance()` has removed study and cell-count effects.

```{r}
de_results <- rowData(pb_se) |>
  tibble::as_tibble(rownames = ".feature") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    gene_symbol = AnnotationDbi::mapIds(
      org.Hs.eg.db,
      keys = stringr::str_replace(.feature, "\\.[0-9]+$", ""),
      keytype = "ENSEMBL",
      column = "SYMBOL",
      multiVals = "first"
    ) |>
      unname() |>
      dplyr::coalesce(.feature)
  )

signature_up <- de_results |>
  dplyr::filter(pvalue < 0.05, log2FoldChange > 0) |>
  dplyr::slice_min(pvalue, n = 25)

signature_down <- de_results |>
  dplyr::filter(pvalue < 0.05, log2FoldChange < 0) |>
  dplyr::slice_min(pvalue, n = 25)

signature_up
```

```{r}
marker_genes <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  dplyr::mutate(signature_up, direction = "up"),
  dplyr::mutate(signature_down, direction = "down")
) |>
  dplyr::select(.feature, gene_symbol, direction)

marker_plot_df <- pb_se[marker_genes$.feature, ] |>
  as_tibble() |>
  dplyr::left_join(marker_genes, by = ".feature")
```

```{r marker-plot}
ggplot(marker_plot_df, aes(age_bin, log1p(counts_adjusted), fill = age_bin)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.4, width = 0.65) +
  facet_wrap(~ gene_symbol + direction, scales = "free_y", ncol = 6) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "none", strip.text = element_text(size = 7)) +
  labs(
    x = "Age",
    y = "log1p(counts_adjusted)",
    title = paste("Cluster", epi_cluster_de_top)
  )
```


> **Exercise 8.** In `de_contrast`, which age class is the numerator? Check one gene in `signature_up` against its boxplot and confirm the direction matches.

<details>
<summary>Solution</summary>

`c("age_binary", "old", "young")` tests old against young. Positive `log2FoldChange` means higher abundance in donors over 50. The boxplot for a gene in `signature_up` should sit higher in the `50-79` bin. If it sits lower, the factor levels and the contrast disagree.

</details>

## Score the ageing signature on single cells

[singscore](https://github.com/DavisLaboratory/singscore) scores each cell by the average rank of the signature genes [@foroutan2018singscore]. The score asks where the age-associated transcriptional change sits inside the chosen cluster. Zero is a cell with no net signature, and a depleted cell stays below zero.

```{r, include=FALSE, eval=TRUE}
sce_epi <- readRDS(file.path(
  dirname(knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE)),
  "..", "inst", "extdata", "sce_epi.rds"
))
```

```{r}
library(singscore)

sce <- sce_epi |>
  dplyr::filter(epi_cluster == epi_cluster_de_top)

rank_mat <- rankGenes(as.matrix(assay(sce, "logcounts")))
sce$aging_signature_score <- simpleScore(
  rank_mat,
  upSet = signature_up$.feature,
  # A threshold test can leave one direction empty; simpleScore needs NULL,
  # not a zero-length vector, and then scores on the up set alone.
  downSet = if (nrow(signature_down) > 0) signature_down$.feature else NULL
)$TotalScore
```

```{r}
sce |>
  ggplot(aes(UMAP1, UMAP2, colour = aging_signature_score)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.3, alpha = 0.6) +
  scale_colour_viridis_c(option = "magma") +
  facet_wrap(~ age_bin, ncol = 2) +
  coord_equal() +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(colour = "Ageing score", title = paste("Cluster", epi_cluster_de_top))
```

```{r}
sce |>
  ggplot(aes(aging_signature_score, fill = age_bin, colour = age_bin)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.35, linewidth = 0.6) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "Ageing signature score", y = "Density", fill = "Age", colour = "Age")
```
